title: Audit Evidence
outcomes: Obtain sufficient appropriate evidence including for specific items.
Audit opening balances in initial engagements.
Audit related party relationships and transactions.

meta.exam_tip: Name the SA, the procedure and the conclusion — in that order.

concepts.title: Sufficient appropriate evidence (SA 500) and specific items (SA 501)
body: Audit evidence must be sufficient (quantity) and appropriate (quality: relevance and reliability). Reliability increases when evidence comes from independent external sources, when controls are effective, when obtained directly by the auditor, when documentary, and when original.

Audit procedures: inspection, observation, external confirmation, recalculation, reperformance, analytical procedures and enquiry. Information produced by the entity must be tested for accuracy and completeness.

SA 501 specifics: attend physical inventory counting when material (observe, inspect, test counts); for litigation and claims, enquire, review minutes and legal expenses, and communicate with external legal counsel where risks exist; for segment information, evaluate methods and disclosures.
concepts.analogy: Better evidence is external, direct, documentary and original.
concepts.work: An auditor attends the stock count rather than relying on management's count sheets.

concepts.title: External confirmations (SA 505)
body: External confirmations are direct written responses from third parties (banks, customers, suppliers, lawyers). The auditor controls the requests: selecting parties, designing and sending requests, and receiving replies directly.

Positive confirmations ask for a reply in every case; negative confirmations ask for a reply only if the recipient disagrees — used only when risk is low, controls effective, population large and homogeneous, and low exception rates are expected.

If management refuses to allow confirmations, the auditor enquires into reasons, evaluates implications, and performs alternative procedures; unreasonable refusal may lead to communication with TCWG and a modified opinion. Non-responses require alternative procedures; exceptions are investigated.
concepts.analogy: The auditor, not the client, controls confirmations.
concepts.work: A missing bank confirmation is a red flag that needs follow-up.

concepts.title: Initial engagements and opening balances (SA 510)
body: In an initial audit engagement, the auditor obtains sufficient evidence that opening balances do not contain misstatements that materially affect current statements, and that accounting policies are applied consistently.

Procedures: read the prior period statements and predecessor's report; review predecessor's working papers; evaluate whether current procedures provide evidence on opening balances; perform specific procedures (e.g. inventory roll-back).
If evidence is insufficient, the opinion is qualified or disclaimed; if prior period report was modified and the matter remains relevant, the current opinion is modified.
concepts.analogy: You inherit last year's closing numbers — verify them.
concepts.work: Opening inventory misstated affects current year profit.

concepts.title: Audit sampling (SA 530)
body: Audit sampling applies procedures to less than 100% of items so that every sampling unit has a chance of selection. Sampling risk (conclusion differs from testing the whole population) and non-sampling risk (wrong procedures, misinterpretation) must be managed.

Design considers the purpose, population, stratification and value-weighted selection; selection methods include random, systematic and monetary unit sampling (haphazard and block selection are less suited to statistical sampling).

Deviations in tests of controls and misstatements in tests of details are evaluated; misstatements are projected to the population and compared with tolerable misstatement. Anomalies may be excluded only with a high degree of certainty that they are not representative.
concepts.analogy: Test part, project to the whole, and allow for sampling risk.
concepts.work: A 4% error rate in sample implies about ₹8 lakh error on ₹200 lakh.

concepts.title: Related parties (SA 550)
body: SA 550 requires understanding related party relationships and transactions, remaining alert for undisclosed ones, and evaluating whether they are properly accounted for and disclosed under the framework.

Risk assessment includes enquiring of management, inspecting records (minutes, contracts, shareholder registers, tax returns), and treating significant related party transactions outside the normal course of business as significant risks.

If new related parties are found, the auditor communicates to the team, asks management to identify all transactions, re-evaluates fraud risk, and performs substantive procedures. Written representations are obtained that all related parties have been disclosed.
concepts.analogy: Related parties can hide transactions not at arm's length.
concepts.work: A large unsecured loan to a director's firm is a significant risk.

illustrations.q: Sales invoices total ₹200 lakh. The auditor tests a sample of invoices worth ₹10 lakh and finds overstatements of ₹0.4 lakh. Tolerable misstatement for sales is ₹10 lakh. Project the misstatement using the ratio method and conclude.

illustrations.q: Handle each: (a) management refuses to let the auditor confirm a major customer; (b) a positive confirmation is not returned; (c) a reply comes from a personal email address; (d) a customer reports a lower balance due to goods returned at year end.

jobs.title: Receivables audit
steps: Send positive confirmations to large balances.
jobs.takeaway: Good sampling plus confirmations gives strong evidence.

summary: SA 550: related parties as significant risks.
traps: Using negative confirmations for high-risk balances.

viva.model: Its relevance and reliability for the assertion being tested.
Positive confirmations ask the party to reply in all cases; negative ones ask for a reply only if they disagree.

viva.q: What procedures apply to opening balances in an initial audit?
viva.model: Reading prior statements and report, reviewing predecessor working papers, and performing specific procedures to obtain evidence.
They are projected to the population and compared with tolerable misstatement, considering sampling risk.

viva.q: What written representation is needed under SA 550?
viva.model: That management has disclosed all known related parties and transactions and accounted for them properly.

cases.title: Prime Distributors Ltd.
cases.case: Prime Distributors stores 30% of its inventory with a third-party warehouse. It faces a ₹5 crore lawsuit from a customer. This is the first year of audit by the current firm; the predecessor issued a qualified opinion on inventory last year. A company owned by the MD's brother bought goods at a 25% discount.

mcqs.q: For third-party held inventory, the auditor should:
options: Confirm with the custodian and/or inspect
mcqs.explain: SA 501. In practice: consider custodian's integrity.
mcqs.topic: Sufficient appropriate evidence (SA 500) and specific items (SA 501)

mcqs.q: For the lawsuit, the auditor should:
options: Seek direct communication with external legal counsel
mcqs.explain: SA 501 litigation procedures. In practice: letter of enquiry.
mcqs.topic: Sufficient appropriate evidence (SA 500) and specific items (SA 501)

mcqs.q: The predecessor's qualification on inventory means:
options: Opening balance evidence and possible current modification must be considered
mcqs.explain: SA 510. In practice: closing inventory of prior year affects profit.

mcqs.q: The discounted sale to the brother's company is:
options: A related party transaction needing scrutiny
mcqs.explain: SA 550 and Ind AS 24. In practice: check approvals.
